cohort: 477 mother-child pairs with children less than 2 years of age
finding: The prevalence of pre-lacteal feeding was 10.1%, and factors associated with this practice included no previous birth, birth spacing less than 24 months, colostrum discarding, less than four antenatal care visits, cesarean section delivery, and maternal belief in the benefits of pre-lacteal feeding.
mod_finding: Mothers who underwent cesarean section were more likely to practice pre-lacteal feeding.
